channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Damascus claims agreement with Moscow over military bases
item.description: Russia and Syria have come to an agreement regarding two military bases along the Middle Eastern coastline. Civilian facilities will be handed back to the Middle Eastern country.

item.title: Paramount agree large-scale deal after Warner Bros takeover
item.description: Grab your popcorns: Paramount will release 30 films a year, to drop in cinemas and streaming services, taking over Warner Bros!

item.title: WHO warehouse hit and destroyed in Ukraine
item.description: A World Health Organization warehouse was damaged in Dnipro, Ukraine, as a result of an attack. A staff member have successfully evacuated almost half of the pallets beforehand.

item.title: Pope calls for protection of civilians amid Sudan war
item.description: Pope Leo XIV visited Sudan on Sunday, where he urged international backing for immadiate ceasefire and pushed for corridors to protect civilians from the war.

item.title: FIFA 'condemns' attempts to oust controversial president
item.description: FIFA has pushed back on calls to remove its President Gianni Infantino, despite being mired in numerous scandals in recent weeks. The organisation refutes all allegations.

item.title: President Zelenskyy fears new large-scale Russian mobilisation
item.description: The combination of an increasing number of North Korean troops and a reluctance to end war on "fair terms" make large-scale attacks possible, Zelenskyy claims.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz can only reopen if US withdraws all troops, Iran says
item.description: Iran demands a hefty compensation fee and complete withdrawal from the United States to consider opening the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Belgium's biggest mining disaster: The black thread connecting Fano and Marcinelle
item.description: Seventy years after the Bois du Cazier disaster, the story of one miner who escaped and another who died reveals how Belgium's coalfields reshaped communities far beyond Wallonia.

item.title: West Nile virus claims over 200 European victims
item.description: Italy and Greece are leading the line with 139 and 61 cases respectively, but two of Belgium's neighbouring countries are also affected.

item.title: Zelenskyy visits Moscow ally with support plea
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy discussed safety and energy support amid intensive ongoing airstrikes from Russian troops.

item.title: German airport installs special radar after drone threat
item.description: The airport is now equipped with an additional checkpoint radar, having recently detected an explosive-laden drone near a Ukrainian aircraft.

item.title: Wildlife management: How Belgian wolves survived ‘attack’ on unprotected sheep
item.description: “The Walloon government is preparing a ‘Wolf Plan’ which signals a policy shift to coexistence with wolves.”

item.title: Dozens of climate activists protest in The Hague after wildfires
item.description: Extinction Rebellion activists blocked a motorway in The Hague in response to the recent drought and wildfires in France, Spain and regions of the Netherlands.

item.title: FIFA denies president mistress bribe allegations
item.description: European football's governing body UEFA uncovered paying a six-figure sum to a mistress of current FIFA President Gianni Infantino. FIFA denies all allegations.

item.title: Amazon builds massive power plant for its AI data centre
item.description: Amazon is building a gas-fired power station in Texas to step up their AI-driven activities, emitting more greenhouse gas than any other building in the US.

item.title: Second World War relics emerge across Europe due to drought
item.description: Low water levels and wildfires have revealed both fascinating and dangerous wartime relics.

item.title: Pope Leo to meet sexual abuse victims during France visit
item.description: The Vatican said the meeting would take place in private.

item.title: Food prices at their highest level in three years, UN says
item.description: Climate disruption weighed heavily on grains, especially wheat.

item.title: Scientists create viruses to combat harmful bacteria using AI, for first time in history
item.description: The researchers said their approach could open the way to phage therapies that can adapt to rapidly evolving pathogens.

item.title: Spanish and French police dismantle major smuggling network with Belgian links
item.description: The network transported drugs from Europe to Algeria, while migrants, drugs and weapons were transported on return.
